defects: The conclusion uses a predicate `Ramified K p` that is not a standard/known Mathlib declaration with this signature (a plain field K and a natural number p) — its meaning is unspecified in the statement itself, so it cannot be confirmed to mean 'the ideal (p) is ramified in the ring of integers of K'.

The produced statement never introduces the ring of integers 𝒪 (or any analogue of gold's `IsIntegralClosure 𝒪 ℤ K`); ramification is stated directly of K and p with no explicit reference to the integral closure, unlike gold which quantifies over an arbitrary ring of integers 𝒪.

Gold's conclusion is phrased as the negation of a well-defined unramifiedness predicate (¬ Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn 𝒪 (Ideal.span {p})); the produced statement asserts a positive but undefined 'Ramified' predicate, so equivalence cannot be verified.

Hypotheses are packaged differently (Field K, Algebra ℚ K, FiniteDimensional ℚ K instead of the bundled NumberField K typeclass); while plausibly equivalent, this repackaging combined with the undefined conclusion predicate makes full equivalence unconfirmable.
